neighbours.label: the word or punctuation that hands over to a cited source's content (This law says…, The leaflet explains…, According to X,)
fire: Newton's first law says an object keeps moving unless a force acts on it.
According to the Oxford dictionary, a sonnet is a poem of fourteen lines.
The leaflet the clinic sent home explains how to prepare for the scan.
The question says: decide which of these sentences use the passive voice.
The manual states that the filter must be replaced every six months.
Here is the puzzle: a farmer has to cross a river with a fox and a goose.
The school rule says students may not use phones during lessons.
As the textbook explains, rainbows form when light bends in raindrops.
quiet: Newton's first law was published in 1687 in a famous book.
The Oxford dictionary sits on the top shelf of the library.
The leaflet the clinic sent home was printed on blue paper.
The question was the hardest one on the whole exam paper.
The manual for the filter got lost when we moved house.
The puzzle took the whole family three evenings to finish.
The school rule was introduced by the new head teacher.
The textbook about rainbows has a bright cover and many photos.

notes: card: ' explains', ' says', ':', ',' after 'According to …', right before the content of a rule or definition
